name: Skylab
dispatch: Skylab was America's first space station, and one of history's great acts of improvisation — an entire orbital workshop built inside the empty hydrogen tank of a spent Saturn V upper stage. Rather than design a station from scratch, NASA converted the hardware the cancelled Moon landings had left over into a house-sized laboratory with crew quarters, a shower, and a crewed solar observatory. Nearly destroyed at launch when its sun shield tore away, it was saved by the first crew's improvised repairs and went on to prove the thing every later station assumed: that people can live and work in orbit for months, and fix their spacecraft when it breaks.
description: America’s first space station, built from a Saturn V S-IVB upper stage. Three crews of three each lived aboard between 1973 and 1974, conducting solar observations and zero-g experiments. Reentered uncontrolled over Australia in 1979.
